title: [BUG-01] HIGH: getGitRemote() fails for proxy-style git remote URLs
description:
## Surface
CLI — `apps/cli/src/git.ts: getGitRemote()`

## Exact command
Any workspace-dependent CLI command in a Claude Code remote environment:
```bash
export DRIFTLESS_API_KEY=drift_...
export DRIFTLESS_API_URL=https://api-staging.driftless.icu
driftless context list
# Error: no git remote found.
```

## Root cause
Git remote URL in managed envs: `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/joseluistello/Driftless`.
`getGitRemote()` sees the `@` in `local_proxy@127.0.0.1` and takes the SSH parsing path. Then splits on `:` — gets `41729/git/joseluistello/Driftless` — 4 segments ≠ 2, returns null.

## Expected
`getGitRemote()` handles standard HTTPS remotes with port numbers (common in managed CI and Claude Code remote envs).

## Actual
```
Error: no git remote found.
```

## Environment
Claude Code remote (cloud); git remote = `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/...`; staging API key set; API blocked by egress policy.

## Severity
HIGH — breaks all CLI commands for any agent in a Claude Code remote env without a prior `driftless login`.

## Suggested validation
1. Set up a git remote with `http://user@host:port/org/repo` format
2. Call `getGitRemote()` directly → confirm it returns null
3. Fix: add HTTPS-with-port parsing branch; use `new URL(clean)` on the `http://` path regardless of `@`

title: [BUG-02] HIGH: Workspace error masks arg validation in all workspace-dependent commands
description:
## Surface
CLI — all commands that call `resolveWorkspaceSlug()` before argument validation

## Exact commands
```bash
driftless context search             # no query → should say "Usage: ..."
driftless collection get             # no id → should say "Error: `collection get <id>`"
driftless broker invoke              # no args → should say "Error: 'broker invoke' needs..."
driftless project get                # no id → same
```

## Expected
Each command prints its specific argument validation error.

## Actual
All print: `Error: no git remote found.`

## Root cause
`resolveWorkspaceSlug()` is invoked at the top of each command handler, before any argument checking. When the API is unreachable AND no workspace is cached AND `getGitRemote()` returns null → process.exit(1) with the git remote error.

## Environment
Staging env with DRIFTLESS_API_KEY set, no prior login, no cached workspace, API unreachable.

## Severity
HIGH — confusing for any agent or user who first sets the API key without running `driftless login`. The error misdirects to git config rather than authentication/connectivity.

## Suggested validation
Without a cached workspace:
1. `driftless context search` with no query
2. `driftless collection get` with no id
3. Check that error messages are command-specific

## Fix candidate
Validate required positional arguments before calling `resolveWorkspaceSlug()`.
acceptance: Running `driftless context search` with no query prints `Usage: driftless context search "<query>"`, not a git error

title: [BUG-03] MEDIUM: git.spec.ts calls live getGitRemote() — fails in proxy git envs
description:
## Surface
CLI unit tests — `apps/cli/src/git.spec.ts:71`

## Exact test
```ts
it('parses standard https and ssh URLs', () => {
  expect(getGitRemote()?.org).toMatch(/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$/)  // calls LIVE git
})
```

## Expected
Test passes regardless of git remote URL format in the test environment.

## Actual
```
TYPEERROR: .toMatch() expects a string, but got undefined
```
Fails in any Claude Code remote environment where the git remote is a proxy URL.

## Environment
CI / Claude Code remote; git remote = `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/...`

## Severity
MEDIUM — breaks `pnpm test` in Claude Code remote environments, reduces trust in the test suite.

## Suggested fix
Mock `execSync` in this test to return known URL strings and test only the parsing logic.
acceptance: CLI unit test suite passes with 213/213 tests in Claude Code remote environments

title: [BUG-04] MEDIUM: context search default limit: CLI says 50, MCP enforces 5 (max 20)
description:
## Surface
CLI help text vs MCP tool schema

## Exact command/call
```bash
# CLI
driftless context search "auth" --json | jq length
# → returns up to 50 (server default)

# MCP
# tools/call driftless_context_search { query: "auth" }
# → returns up to 5 (MCP default)
```

## CLI help says
```
--limit <n>   Cap results server-side (server hard-caps at 50; default 50)
```

## MCP tool schema
```ts
// apps/mcp/src/tools/tool-registry.ts
const DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT = 5
const MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT = 20
```

## Expected
Consistent defaults and maximums across CLI and MCP, or the difference is explicitly documented.

## Actual
- CLI: default 50, max 50 (server hard cap)
- MCP: default 5, max 20 (MCP-enforced, not server)
- CLI help says "server hard-caps at 50" which is now a lie for MCP users

## Severity
MEDIUM — an agent switching from CLI to MCP sees 10x fewer results for the same query. Could cause false "no results" conclusions and agents writing notes that the team already has documented.

## Suggested validation
1. `driftless context search "auth" --json | jq length`
2. MCP `driftless_context_search { query: "auth" }` → check count
3. Compare
acceptance: CLI and MCP context search have documented, consistent limits. CLI help text matches actual behavior.

title: [BUG-05] MEDIUM: driftless_broker MCP tool hidden by default with no discoverability
description:
## Surface
MCP — `tools/list`

## Exact request
```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}
```

## Expected
Either `driftless_broker` appears in `tools/list`, or the response carries a `next_action` hint about how to enable it.

## Actual
`driftless_broker` is silently absent unless `DRIFTLESS_BROKER_ENABLED=true` is set server-side. No hint in any other tool's response. No mention in `tools/list` metadata.

## Code
```ts
// apps/mcp/src/tools/tool-registry.ts
if (!this.brokerEnabled()) {
  this.tools = this.tools.filter((tool) => tool.name !== 'driftless_broker')
}
```

## Environment
Staging with broker feature flag off (default).

## Severity
MEDIUM — an agent using only MCP has no way to discover the broker surface exists. The CLI shows it; MCP silently omits it. An agent that should use broker will instead try to script raw HTTP calls.

## Suggested validation
1. `tools/list` on staging → confirm broker absent, no hint
2. Enable flag → confirm broker appears

## Fix candidates
a) Always include `driftless_broker` in `tools/list` but return a 503 with a clear message on call when disabled
b) Add a `feature_flags` field to the `driftless_workspaces` or `driftless_areas` tool result noting that broker is available
acceptance: An agent calling tools/list can discover whether broker is available (and how to request it) without reading CLI help

title: [BUG-06] MEDIUM: collection records --status without --limit uses legacy unbounded endpoint
description:
## Surface
CLI — `apps/cli/src/commands/collection.ts`

## Exact command
```bash
driftless collection records <collection-id> --status in_progress
# Returns ALL records with status=in_progress — no nextCursor emitted
```

## CLI help claims
`collection records <collection-id> [--status <stage>] [--limit <n>] [--cursor <token>]   # bounded server-side; follow nextCursor to page`

## Actual behavior
When only `--status` is given (no `--limit` or `--cursor`):
```ts
// apps/cli/src/commands/collection.ts:110-124
// --status alone keeps the legacy bare-array shape; unwrap handles both.
```
The legacy bare-array endpoint has no server-side bound. 1,000 records in status=in_progress returns all 1,000.

## Expected
Help text should warn that `--status` alone is unbounded; or a default limit should be applied even for status-only queries.

## Severity
MEDIUM — an agent filtering a large collection by status gets an unbounded dump. Help text says "bounded server-side" which is misleading.

## Suggested validation
1. Collection with 100+ records all in `in_progress` status
2. `driftless collection records <id> --status in_progress` → observe record count and absence of nextCursor

## Fix candidate
Always send a default limit (e.g. 50) even for status-only queries; remove the legacy bare-array path.
acceptance: collection records --status X without --limit either warns about unbounded query or applies a default limit and emits nextCursor

title: [BUG-07] LOW: Broker subcommand --help shows parent help (no per-subcommand help)
description:
## Surface
CLI — `apps/cli/src/commands/broker.ts`

## Exact commands
```bash
driftless broker connections --help    # → full broker help
driftless broker operations --help     # → full broker help (--refresh not highlighted)
driftless broker invoke --help         # → full broker help (--input not highlighted)
driftless broker records --help        # → full broker help
```

## Expected
Each subcommand shows help relevant to itself, e.g. `broker connections --help` should say "Lists connected providers. No extra flags needed."

## Actual
All subcommands with `--help` produce identical full-broker-help output.

## Root cause
```ts
if (flags['help'] === true || sub === 'help') { printHelp(); process.exit(0) }
```
The help check is before the subcommand switch.

## Severity
LOW — not a crash. An agent running `broker operations --help` to learn about `--refresh` gets the full help dump, which includes the answer, but the UX is poor.

## Suggested validation
Run each subcommand with `--help`; observe identical output.
acceptance: broker subcommand --help produces output specific to that subcommand, or is documented as intentional

title: [BUG-08] MEDIUM: MCP driftless_project action:'list' has no limit — all projects returned
description:
## Surface
MCP — `driftless_project`

## Exact call
```json
{"name":"driftless_project","arguments":{"action":"list"}}
```

## Expected
Paginated response with `has_more`/`next_action` hint; or documented that all projects are returned.

## Actual
```ts
// apps/mcp/src/tools/tool-registry.ts
case 'list': {
  const status = typeof args['status'] === 'string' ? args['status'] : 'active'
  return this.api.get(`/workspaces/${workspace}/projects?status=${encodeURIComponent(status)}`, ctx)
}
```
No `limit`; no `has_more`; entire project list returned. A workspace with 200 active projects returns them all.

## Severity
MEDIUM — context flooding for large workspaces; pattern inconsistent with `driftless_context_list` which has has_more/hint.

## Suggested validation
Create 50+ projects on staging; call `driftless_project { action: 'list' }` → observe count and absence of has_more.

## Fix
Add `limit`/`offset` to schema; wrap response in `{ items, count, has_more }` envelope.
acceptance: driftless_project action:'list' returns has_more:true when more projects exist, with a next_action hint

title: [BUG-09] LOW-MEDIUM: MCP driftless_collection action:'list' has no limit
description:
## Surface
MCP — `driftless_collection`

## Exact call
```json
{"name":"driftless_collection","arguments":{"action":"list"}}
```

## Actual
```ts
case 'list': {
  const query = this.queryString(args, ['status'])
  return this.api.get(`/workspaces/${workspace}/collections${query}`, ctx)
}
```
No limit parameter; no `has_more`.

## Comparison
`driftless_areas action:'list'` uses a hard 40-item client-side cap. `driftless_collection action:'list'` has none.

## Severity
LOW-MEDIUM — inconsistent with the rest of the MCP surface.

## Suggested fix
Add `limit` param; emit `{ items, count, has_more }` envelope.
acceptance: driftless_collection action:'list' is bounded (default 40) and consistent with other list tools

title: [BUG-10] LOW: Smoke test uses non-workspace-scoped /topics/retrieve endpoint
description:
## Surface
Smoke test harness — `scripts/harness/smoke.sh`

## Exact request in smoke test
```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $SMOKE_KEY" \
  -d '{"query":"smoke","files":["src/smoke/probe.ts"],"limit":1}' \
  "$SMOKE_URL/api/v1/topics/retrieve"
```

## MCP tool uses
```ts
this.api.post(`/workspaces/${workspace}/topics/retrieve`, body, ctx)
// → POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/topics/retrieve
```

## Issue
The smoke test verifies the bare `/api/v1/topics/retrieve` endpoint (no workspace in path), while the actual MCP-called endpoint is `/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/topics/retrieve`. If the server infers workspace from the auth key for the bare endpoint, the smoke test passes but doesn't verify the actual MCP code path.

## Severity
LOW — may not be a bug if both endpoints work and are equivalent. Needs verification.

## Suggested validation
1. Call both endpoints with same payload on staging
2. Verify both return 200 and the same response shape
3. If bare endpoint is a different code path, update smoke to test the workspace-scoped one
acceptance: Smoke test exercises the same endpoint the MCP tool calls, or documents that both paths are equivalent

title: [BUG-11] LOW-MEDIUM: context list --suggested and --all fetch unbounded from server
description:
## Surface
CLI — `apps/cli/src/commands/context.ts`

## Exact commands
```bash
driftless context list --suggested --json | jq length   # unbounded
driftless context list --all --json | jq length         # unbounded
```

## Expected
Either a server-side limit is applied, or the user/agent is warned when the workspace has many topics.

## Actual
```ts
// apps/cli/src/commands/context.ts:325
const canBoundServerSide = !flags['suggested'] && !flags['all']
// When --suggested or --all: NO limit sent to server
```
For a workspace with 10,000 topics, `--all --json` fetches all 10,000 then sorts/slices client-side.

## Severity
LOW-MEDIUM — performance/memory risk for large workspaces; `--suggested` is likely to be used in agent loops.

## Suggested validation
On a staging workspace with 500+ topics:
1. `driftless context list --suggested --json | jq length`
2. Measure response time and memory usage

## Fix
For `--suggested`: query server for draft/proposed status (if API supports it) to avoid full-workspace fetch. For `--all`: add a warning when result set exceeds a threshold.
acceptance: context list --suggested does not fetch the entire workspace; or a warning is emitted when result count exceeds 200
